opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jacob Ellison (employee ID E040) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E040.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jacob Ellison (E040) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested admin to Source Code, but Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted for this role. Maximum allowable is write; recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E040 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors without advanced training max out at read; admin is never permitted for contractors. Recommend granting read.
reason: HR database (authoritative for employment type) lists Jacob Ellison (E040) as a full-time Payroll Specialist. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, not Payroll Specialist, so admin is not permitted regardless. For full-time employees the maximum allowable access is write. The requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum, so grant the maximum of write.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Jacob Ellison (E040) requests admin access to Source Code.

Notes:
- HR: role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time. Recommendation: write. Source Code owned by Engineer role, so admin not permitted; max write.
- Security: role Payroll Specialist (not looked up), employment type contractor, security training basic. Recommendation: read. Contractors without advanced training max at read.

Conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor.

Who should I trust? The HR agent looked up employment type in their own database. The Security agent looked up employment type in their own database. Both claim to have looked it up. Hmm.

The HR note says employment type full_time (looked up in own database). Security says contractor (looked up in own database). Conflicting.

We need to decide. The access policy: full_time employees up to write, admin only if role owns system. Payroll Specialist role doesn't own Source Code (Engineer owns it), so max write. Contractor: read or write if advanced training; never admin. Security says basic training, so max read.

Requested admin. If full_time: max write → grant write. If contractor with basic: max read → grant read.

Which employment type to believe? HR's database is authoritative for employment type presumably. But Security looked it up too. The note says Security "looked up in own database before writing" for employment type. Hmm, both looked up in "own database." 

Generally, HR is the authority on employment type. HR says full_time. So employee is full-time Payroll Specialist. Max is write. Requested admin is above max, so grant write.

Alternatively, consider conflict resolution: HR is authoritative for employment/role. Security is authoritative for security training. So full_time + basic training — for full_time employees, training doesn't matter. Max write (admin only if role owns system, not the case). Grant write.

So decision: write.

Let me submit write with reasoning.
